title: Backyard Party Planning Kit
subtitle: Measure your yard, size your party, and plan shade, power, restrooms, and cleanup
intro: A backyard party can feel effortless, but it takes a little math to get right. This kit starts with measuring your space and then walks through seating, shade, power, restrooms, neighbors, food, rentals, and cleanup.

sections.heading: Yard Measuring and Party Worksheet
sections.note: Sketch your yard on the back of this page and mark each item below.
fields: Gate or path width for deliveries
Where the food will be set up

sections.heading: Space Per Guest
sections.note: Rough planning numbers. Allow more room for dancing, games, or lots of kids.
rows: Seated with buffet and lawn games
Allow 10 to 15 ft of table space

tasks: Choose a date and a backup date if the weather is uncertain.
Measure the yard and decide on the number of guests.
Check city or village rules for tents, noise, fires, and street parking.
Request rental quotes for tent, tables, chairs, and linens.
Think through restroom, power, and lighting needs.
Choose a food style: grill, catering, food truck, or potluck.
Send invitations with start and end times and parking notes.
Book rentals and confirm delivery windows.
Hire a caterer, bartender, or food truck if needed.
Order a cake or desserts.
Reserve a portable restroom if needed.
Plan games, music, and activities.
Follow up on RSVPs.
Notify neighbors about the party, noise, and parking.
Mow, trim, and treat the lawn for bugs if needed.
Check the sprinkler schedule and turn it off for the party.
Buy drinks, ice, and paper goods.
Test string lights and extension cords.
Watch the forecast and decide on the tent or rain plan.
Give the final headcount to the caterer.
Prep make-ahead food.
Mark delivery spots and clear paths for rentals.
Set up coolers and ice plan.
Prepare a cleanup plan and trash bags.
Set up tables and chairs at least 2 hours before guests arrive.
Test lighting and music.
Put out bug spray, sunscreen, and water.
Check restrooms and supplies.
Keep food covered and cold until serving.
Greet guests and relax.
Bag trash and recycling promptly.
Stack rentals as instructed for pickup.
Check the lawn for litter, glass, and decorations.
Thank neighbors with a note or small treat.
Send photos and thank-yous.

groups.title: Tent and shade
items: Decide if you need a tent for rain, sun, or both.
Choose a tent size based on the table layout.
Ask about staking vs weights if you have a patio or concrete.
Check overhead trees and wires.
Plan shade for the food table and older guests.
Consider umbrellas or pop-up canopies for smaller areas.

groups.title: Power
items: Identify outlets and which circuit breakers they use.
Avoid overloading circuits with coolers, speakers, and lights.
Use outdoor-rated extension cords.
Tape or cover cords to prevent tripping.
Plan battery or solar options for lighting.
Know where the breaker panel is.

groups.title: Lighting
items: String lights over the eating area.
Path lights for steps and gates.
Lanterns or candles in safe containers.
Lighting near the bar and food area.
Bug-repelling candles or fans.
A flashlight or two for emergencies.

groups.title: Restrooms
items: Plan on one restroom per 25 to 30 guests for a short party, and more for longer events.
Stock extra toilet paper, soap, and hand towels.
Mark the path to the indoor bathroom.
Consider a portable restroom for 50 or more guests.
Add a trash can and a small light.

groups.title: Neighbors
items: Tell neighbors about the date and hours.
Share your phone number in case of concerns.
Know your local noise rules and quiet hours.
Point speakers away from neighbors' homes.
Keep the party to the agreed end time.

groups.title: Parking and arrival
items: Check street parking rules and any permits.
Reserve a driveway spot for deliveries and vendors.
Share parking tips and rideshare options.
Create a clear pathway from the street to the yard.
Set up signage for the gate or entrance.

sections.heading: Food and Drink Amounts
sections.note: Rough guidelines for a 3 to 4 hour party. Adjust for heat, appetite, and the mix of kids and adults.
rows: Burgers, hot dogs, or main proteins

groups.title: Seating and tables
items: Chairs for about 60 to 70 percent of guests at one time.
Round or banquet tables for dining.
Cocktail tables for mingling.
A kids' table with smaller chairs.
Lounge furniture for a relaxed corner.
Linens in a color that hides spills.

groups.title: Food and drink equipment
items: Chafing dishes and fuel.
Drink dispensers and tubs.
Plates, cutlery, and glassware if not using disposables.
Grill or smoker if you do not own one.
Extra coolers.
Serving utensils.

groups.title: Weather and fun
items: Tent or canopy.
Patio heaters for cool evenings.
Fans for hot days.
Dance floor or flooring over grass.
Lawn games and a small stage if needed.
String lights and pole supports.

sections.heading: Cleanup Plan
items: Place trash, recycling, and compost bins in obvious spots, with extra bags nearby.
Assign two helpers to empty bins during the party.
Keep a small bucket for tableware to avoid scattering items.
Before the party ends, ask guests to take home leftover food in containers you provide.
Return rentals clean and dry, following the rental company's instructions.
Walk the lawn with a bag and a magnet to pick up bits you missed.
Run the dishwasher or hand-wash glassware the next morning.
Take down string lights and decor in daylight.

sections.heading: Budget Split
sections.note: Rough shares. Backyard parties usually cost less than renting a venue.

lines.tip: Mix catering with self-serve sides to keep costs down.
Buy water and soda in bulk.
Share portable restroom costs if you can.
String lights make a big impact.
A playlist and speaker can be enough.
Buy extra trash bags and gloves.
Keep a little aside for ice or a last-minute need.
